source_text: In traditional or non-medical khitan practices, particularly in rural or community-based settings in Muslim-majority regions, anesthesia use can be inconsistent or absent, resulting in heightened acute pain and potential long-term behavioral effects like altered pain thresholds, as evidenced by observational studies on unanesthetized circumcisions. [44]
